g.text: The recommended stop, and a claim button
Never blank this screen because the news is bad. “Trafalgar at 94%, and it is your only option” is actionable; null is not — that is trap 8, on a phone.
The clocks those states are reacting to
Four HOS clocks and one weight gate — all read-only in Admin, because a compliance product that lets you edit the law is lying. And below them, for contrast, the one number here that is editable.

text.font-family: Roboto Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

g.text: The clock drivers already watch. Runs only while the truck is moving.

text.font-family: Roboto Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

g.text: A dock wait burns this while the truck is stationary — which is why detention and HOS share a screen.

text.font-family: Roboto Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

g.text: The interesting one: it can expire while the truck is parked. No other clock we model does that.

text.font-family: Roboto Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

g.text: A carrier-level choice, so it is set once in Admin and never during a shift.

text.font-family: Roboto Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

g.text: Paired with HOS as one pre-dispatch audit: canAccept returns both kinds of reason from a single call.

text.font-family: Roboto Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

g.text: The one editable number on this list. It is a contract term, not a law, so it belongs to whoever signs the contract.
An HOS warning with no parking answer is half a product — which is why state C leads with a place to stop rather than a countdown.
The load leads. Accept / Reject is a real veto,
and the compliance gate ran before the offer.
The detention clock leads — it is the driver’s
leverage while they can still escalate.
Parking takes the top and the load card drops.
Never blank the screen because the news is bad.

g.text: This inverts every legacy TMS, and it is the first thing to show a judge. Parking and the 49-row road-conditions list are
deliberately gone from the front page — they stay in the engine and reach this desk only inside a queue card.
EXCEPTION · ONLY THE LEFT COLUMN CHANGES
Same shell, one card. Satellite is on because the dispatcher is inspecting yard access; breadcrumbs and the speed trace are
folds over pings we already store, and they live one click from a truck rather than crowding the front page.

g.text: To change anything, edit design/board.mjs and re-run
node design/board.mjs — the svg is generated, not drawn.
The Figma MCP connector is not authorised in this workspace, so this
board ships as an svg rather than being written into a file directly.
Dark only — read in a cab, and in a demo room with the lights up. src/styles.css sets color-scheme: dark and never offers a light theme.
THE DECISION LOG IS THE POINT
“Why did truck 118 get that load” has an answer on screen instead of in someone’s head. planAssignments already computes the losing
candidates on its way to the winner — it just has to stop throwing them away. The policy toggle lives here, not on a dispatcher’s shift.
It is their dock causing it and their invoice at
the end. A live counter turns a month-end billing
dispute into a fact both sides watched happen.

g.text: Their own clock, running, before the invoice arrives.
One engine number — billableMin = max(0, dwellMin − 120) at FTL stop sites — rendered four ways. Rest areas never bill.
What each region on these frames is judged under
The layouts above were not chosen by taste. Every region earns one of the brief’s seven criteria, or it is not on the frame.
Axle-weight line in the offer card
7 · can it replace the fragmented tools
Parking and the road-conditions list are deliberately absent from the dispatcher front page: they reach that desk only inside a queue card.
EDITABLE: COMMERCIAL TERMS WE CHOSE. READ-ONLY: LAW, PHYSICS, OR A STATED ASSUMPTION.
A console that offered the read-only inputs anyway would be lying about what it controls — so every field says which of the two it is, inline.
Every administrator action is appended to the same event log, so the audit trail costs a fold rather than a table.
